titulo.texto: Walk: the climb to El Rey

frase_gancho.texto: A short stretch to listen to as you climb.

puente_narrativo.texto: You have arrived at El Rey.

guion_corto.texto: Now climb the slope. High on the hill is the relief that Eulalia Guzmán studied first, in nineteen thirty-four, when the rains left it exposed. As you walk, remember that the reliefs here stand several meters apart and cannot be seen all together. You have to go from one to the next. There is also a stream that carries rainwater down the slope, near the highest reliefs. When you arrive at a scene with a person seated in a cave, you are already in the next audio.

guion_largo.texto:
This is a walk. There is no need to stop. Climb calmly up the slope while the audio keeps you company.

High on the hill is the relief that Eulalia Guzmán studied first, in nineteen thirty-four. Torrential rains had caused a landslide and left it exposed. Today we know it as Monument One, El Rey.

As you climb, keep in mind that the reliefs here stand several meters apart. To see them you have to move along the slope, and perhaps that is how it was done in ancient times.

Near the highest reliefs runs a stream that carries rainwater down the slope. That water and those stones share a theme, as you will see.

When you arrive at a scene with a person seated in a cave, you are already in the next audio.

texto: Climb slowly and look at the rock of the hill
Look for the stream that runs down the slope
Stop when you see a scene with a cave
